plan.summary:
New `Record` IDs now use UUIDv7, which sorts by creation time, instead of random UUIDv4.

- `Cargo.toml` swaps the `uuid` feature `v4` for `v7`.
- `Record::new` calls `Uuid::now_v7()` instead of `Uuid::new_v4()`.
- `Cargo.lock` adds `js-sys` to `getrandom` and `rand` to `uuid`.

Existing records keep their old IDs.
plan.riskRationale: Small change with a one-line behavior switch. Only IDs of newly created records change. The feature swap removes `v4`, so any other `new_v4` call would stop compiling.
plan.storyArc: The PR switches ID generation to time-ordered UUIDv7. First the dependency feature is changed so the API exists. Then `Record::new` uses it. The lockfile edits are the resolver's result.

topics.title: Generate Record IDs as time-ordered UUIDv7
topics.narrativeBrief: How do new Record IDs change, and what enables it? Connect the `v7` feature flag in Cargo.toml to the `Uuid::now_v7()` call in `Record::new`. Verify no other `new_v4` caller remains, since the `v4` feature is removed.
